key_insight: A message-passing reinforcement learning architecture coordinates global and node-level network control while preserving permutation symmetries and transparency constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports scalable control of interconnected systems, including joint decisions about intervention budgets and institution-level capital allocations in financial networks.
method: Use message passing with separate global and local policy heads.
Derive explicit Lipschitz bounds for parameter and input perturbations.
Use these bounds to establish projected policy-gradient convergence guarantees.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on systemic-risk management report better performance than feedforward-network baselines and scalability to large networks, though the abstract provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Sensitivity and optimization behavior depend on architectural choices and graph characteristics, so robustness should be checked for each deployment setting.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
